turns.content: hey, so i finally looked up the exact wording of the guild charter. section 4 says: "any person attending five (5) sanctioned weekend sessions within a rolling eight-week window qualifies as an active guild member, with full voting rights on library acquisitions." and i've got my notes... i went june 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29. all saturdays, all sanctioned sessions. so that's five in a row, right? but then julian mentioned new members usually wait for an email invite, which made me second-guess myself. am i reading this wrong? also, honestly, showing up five weekends straight was kind of a big deal for me — i'm pretty introverted so it took a lot of planning to keep going.

You're reading it right. Five sessions, five consecutive Saturdays, all within an eight-week window — you hit the charter's requirement exactly. June 1 through 29 spans five weeks, well inside the rolling window.

Julian's email-invite comment sounds like informal custom rather than charter language. Nothing in the wording you quoted says membership activates only via email — it says attending five sessions *qualifies* you. So a reasonable read is that you're already qualified, and the email is just how they typically confirm or onboard people. If you want to be safe, you could nudge whoever keeps attendance records and ask them to confirm your five sessions are logged. That turns "I think I qualify" into "the record shows I qualify."

And genuinely — five weekends in a row when you're introverted is no small thing. That's not just showing up, that's sustained follow-through on something that took real effort each time. You earned the voting rights twice over: once by the charter's math, and once by everything it took to get there.

yeah, that's what i thought too but then julian's comment just kinda hung in my head. thanks for confirming i'm not crazy 🤔

so the next vote is like ten days away. do i just show up? or should i say something to julian first

You're definitely not crazy — Julian's comment probably just reflects how things usually go for people who drift in slowly, not someone who hit five straight in a tight window. You compressed the process, so the usual pattern doesn't quite match your case.

For the vote: **say something to Julian first.** Not because you need permission, but because it'll make everything smoother. Something low-key like, "Hey, I've been tracking my attendance — I hit five sessions in the June window, so I believe I'm active under Section 4. Just wanted to confirm before the vote on [date]." That gives him a heads-up, puts it on record, and lets him flag any procedural stuff (like if they maintain a member roll he needs to update).

Then show up. You don't need to wait for the email invite — the charter doesn't say "qualifies pending email confirmation," it says attending five sessions qualifies you. But giving Julian notice avoids that awkward moment where someone questions your standing mid-meeting and you have to litigate it on the spot. Way easier to resolve over text ten days out.

You've already done the hard part five weekends running. One short message is nothing.
yeah, that makes sense. i'll message julian tonight then. short and simple, like you said. maybe just ask him to check the attendance log before the vote.

That's a solid move — asking him to check the log makes it objective instead of "trust me, I was there." Takes the pressure off both of you.

One small tip: send it with enough lead time that if there's any hiccup (like a session didn't get logged), you have a few days to sort it out before the vote. Tonight works great for that.

You've got this handled. Go send that message.
yeah ok i think i will message him tonight. just a quick note asking him to check the log before the vote. short and simple is good. thanks

Perfect. Short and simple, done tonight, and then you can stop turning it over in your head.

Good luck — and enjoy the vote. You earned your seat at that table.
yeah i sent him a quick message. just asked if he could check the log before the vote. we'll see what he says 🤷

Nice, done and dusted. Now it's in his court, and you've got the charter text in your back pocket if you need it.

That 🤷 energy is right — you did your part, the rest is just waiting. Either he confirms and you're set, or he comes back with something weird and you deal with it then. No point pre-stressing about a response that probably amounts to "yep, all good."

Enjoy the next ten days knowing you're in.
